blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 2 killings of trans people in 2025 on a population of ~3.3 million, a rate of about 0.61 per million per year, in a year the country recorded 80 such killings overall. The monitoring dossiers track a broad regional concentration: one contiguous bloc of states absorbed roughly 38 of the 80 killings in 2025, and this state/province itself recorded 6 in 2024, placing it in that year's highest state totals, so its absolute number swung sharply between dossiers. At this population a single additional case would move the rate dramatically.

No unit-specific legal restriction or enforcement finding was identified; the profile rests on the per-capita count, the 2024 toll and the regional concentration. A neighbouring state/province of similar size recorded 4 killings in 2025.
blindSourceSummaries: The national trans-association's 9th annual dossier (released 26 Jan 2026, reported by a national broadcaster): the country recorded 80 murders of trans and transfeminine people in 2025, 34% down on 2024 but with at least 75 attempted homicides and crimes marked by excessive violence; per-state 2025 counts run from two states at 8 each and two at 7 each through three at 5 each, one other state at 3, and this state/province at 2; 1,261 murders over 2017-2025 (avg 140/year); 97% of victims transfeminine people or trans women, over half aged 18-29, 70% black among racially-identified cases; 67.5% of killings happened in interior cities rather than capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policies are harder; the country has led the global ranking since 2008. Gives this state/province's 2025 count (2) within the per-state ranking.

National broadsheet coverage of the same dossier (27 Jan 2025): the country led global trans-murder tallies for the 16th consecutive year with 122 killings in 2024, a 16% fall on 2023; victim profile predominantly young, black, poor and concentrated in the same large regional bloc, with the population's life expectancy cited at about 35 years; most murders happen in public places, at night, with extreme cruelty; authorities rarely register victims' gender identity, degrading official data; the state-by-state 2024 table ranges from 2 killings in one state through 5 each in two states to 6 in this state/province and 8 in another; the national association's president demands effective public policies and honest statistics. Shows this state/province recorded 6 killings in 2024, among the highest state totals that year.
